content.title: About
content.content: Chili is a spicy sauce made from tomatoes, chili peppers and spices, specially formulated for vegetarians. It contains no meat, fish or seafood, yet delivers the rich, piquant flavor typical of traditional chili.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The heat comes from capsaicin, the active compound in chili peppers.
Vegetarian versions often include beans or tofu to boost protein content.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are a great source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Chili pairs well with Mexican dishes but also works great on pasta, rice and vegetable plates.
There are many heat levels – from mild to extreme ghost‑pepper heat.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Capsaicin may increase metabolic rate and help burn calories.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes and peppers provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Antioxidant source
items.content: Lycopene and other phytochemicals protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Capsaicin can promote vasodilation and improve circulation.

items.title: Plant‑based protein
items.content: Added beans or tofu raise the protein content, important for vegetarians.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot sauce may irritate the stomach or esophagus in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some people are allergic to tomatoes or peppers.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain high salt levels; people with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Capsaicin can enhance the effects of certain anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add chili to vegetarian tacos, burritos, soups, stews, pasta, rice dishes and vegetable casseroles. For milder heat, thin the sauce with plant‑based yogurt or milk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in a sealed jar in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks. For longer storage, freeze in small containers.
